title: South Korea launches joint inspection after hack of government administrative email system
date_note: Date of the ministry's release; the ministry says it was notified of the hack on 9 November.
org: Ministry of the Interior and Safety / National Information Resources Service
summary: South Korea's Interior Ministry says related agencies told it on 9 November that the administrative email system run by the National Information Resources Service was hacked; about 300 accounts showed abnormal access. The attacker came through some local governments' weak networks and used a single sign-on flaw. The ministry reported the leak to the privacy regulator, notified those affected, began a joint inspection with NIS and KISA and aims to find the cause by year-end.
plain: Hackers got into South Korean government work email accounts through a login flaw. The ministry has cut connections, told the people affected and is investigating.
exec: Shows how a weak local network and shared single sign-on can expose a national government system.
action: General advice: review single sign-on and the links between partner or local networks and your email system; look for abnormal sign-ins.

sources.name: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (korea.kr)

validation.note: Government press release (primary source) plus Byline Network (16 Nov), which reports the ministry's statement including the NIRS-run email system and the year-end target for the cause; the attacker is not named. korea.kr did not load on 22 Nov (ECONNRESET).
